analysis:
Reviewed the add-on hold changes in ProviderLoop+Serve.swift and ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift.

Serve.swift: the early-exit checks at head lines 26, 81, 93, 135, 204, 227 and 235 now use `servingDrain.refusingForServiceChange` instead of `servingDrain.refusing`. An add-on hold therefore no longer ends startup: the provider still registers, and refusal is moved to inference admission.

`startAddonHoldService()` (head line 76) runs before security hardening, the local endpoint (line 107) and the startup preload gate (line 133). This matches the stated intent that admission closes before any model load.

StartupPreload.swift (head lines 195-197): the change only adds a log line. The existing `!servingDrain.refusing` guard still returns `.cancelled` under a hold, so no preload task starts. run() then continues to registration.

Security-sensitive registration paths are unchanged: the attestation provider (lines 592-614), the fixed-key App Attest resume responder (lines 217-219), and the connection-control reader that clears authorization on connect/disconnect (lines 414-435). No T-053/TB-011 binding or revocation semantics changed, and no encryption or cache (T-041) paths were touched.

Unverified contracts for integration:
- The `refusingForServiceChange` and `owner == .addonHold` semantics live in ServingDrain, which was not supplied. Confirm that an add-on hold makes `refusing` true and `refusingForServiceChange` false.
- Confirm that inference admission (handleInferenceRequest / admitInWorkFIFO), the local endpoint, load_model, prefetch and desired_models all reject work while the hold is active.
- Confirm that the quote/`slot_state` advertisement reflects the hold, so a registered but held provider does not attract routed work it then fails (availability only).

No concrete security regression was identified.
